 NBL27 Round 10 Predictions & Tips
 November 16 th 2026, 12:50pm , By: Heath Chick 
 The 2026/27 NBL season moves into Round 10 with seven games across five days, beginning with New Zealand Breakers hosting South East Melbourne Phoenix in Wednesday night's Ignite Cup clash.
 There are several important matchups this week, including Illawarra Hawks hosting Adelaide 36ers, Cairns Taipans facing Perth Wildcats and Melbourne United taking on New Zealand. The round concludes on Sunday with Brisbane Bullets hosting Sydney Kings.
 We'll have full betting previews for five games across Round 10: Breakers v Phoenix, Hawks v 36ers, Taipans v Wildcats, United v Breakers and Bullets v Kings. Our analysis and betting selections for Tasmania JackJumpers v Illawarra Hawks and Phoenix v Taipans will be available directly on this page, with odds and injury updates added throughout the week.

 NBL27 Round 10 Predictions & Tips 
 Here's our game-by-game look at Round 10 of NBL27. We'll publish separate betting previews for five games, while the remaining two matchups will have their analysis and selections updated directly on this page.
 FULL MATCH PREVIEW 
 New Zealand Breakers v South East Melbourne Phoenix
 WED 18 NOV | 5:30pm AEDT | Spark Arena, Auckland 
 New Zealand host South East Melbourne on Wednesday night with an intriguing new addition to their lineup, having signed former Phoenix import Skylar Mays. The American guard will make an immediate return against the club that released him earlier this month, adding plenty of spice to this Ignite Cup encounter. The Breakers have struggled for consistency, particularly following Parker Jackson-Cartwright's season-ending injury, but Mays' arrival provides much-needed backcourt depth and another scoring option alongside Sam Mennenga and Dejan Vasiljevic.
 South East Melbourne will be looking to bounce back from a disappointing run of results, with defensive inconsistency continuing to undermine their considerable offensive talent. Nathan Sobey remains their most dangerous scoring threat, supported by D'Shawn Schwartz, Angus Glover and emerging youngster Dash Daniels. The Phoenix's decision to release Mays has created additional opportunities for their remaining guards, although facing their former teammate just days after his departure adds an interesting subplot to an already important contest.
 Mays' familiarity with South East Melbourne's personnel and playing style could provide New Zealand with a useful advantage, although his limited preparation time with the Breakers is an important consideration. The Phoenix have enough firepower to challenge New Zealand, but their defensive struggles and the Breakers' home-court advantage make this a difficult matchup. Much will depend on how quickly Mays settles into his new surroundings and whether South East Melbourne can produce a more disciplined defensive performance.
 FULL PREVIEW ->  
 FULL MATCH PREVIEW 
 Illawarra Hawks v Adelaide 36ers
 THU 19 NOV | 7:30pm AEDT | WIN Entertainment Centre, Wollongong 
 Illawarra return home on Thursday night looking to build on some encouraging recent offensive performances. The Hawks have struggled to find consistency throughout the opening rounds, but victories over Perth, Cairns and South East Melbourne have demonstrated their ability to score heavily when their attacking combinations are working. Kelan Martin, Tyler Harvey and Makur Maker provide several dangerous scoring options, while Will Hickey's playmaking has become increasingly important to their offensive structure.
 Adelaide arrive with renewed confidence after their impressive 101-93 victory over Melbourne United in Round 9. The 36ers produced a dominant opening half, establishing a remarkable 34-point advantage before surviving United's spirited comeback. Bryce Cotton remains one of the competition's most influential offensive players, but Adelaide's ability to generate contributions from across the lineup was particularly encouraging against Melbourne. Coach Trevor Gleeson will be hoping that performance provides the foundation for a more consistent run of results.
 The Hawks have already recorded a convincing 114-92 victory over Adelaide this season, although the 36ers will be determined to reverse that result. Illawarra's offensive potential makes them dangerous at home, but their defensive inconsistency remains a concern against a team featuring Cotton. Adelaide's improved confidence and the Hawks' ability to control the rebounding battle should be central to this matchup.
 FULL PREVIEW -> 
 FULL MATCH PREVIEW 
 Cairns Taipans v Perth Wildcats
 FRI 20 NOV | 7:30pm AEDT | Cairns Convention Centre 
 Cairns enter Round 10 full of confidence after consecutive victories over Perth and Sydney, including a remarkable comeback against the ladder-leading Kings. The Taipans overturned a 21-point halftime deficit to claim an 84–82 victory, holding Sydney to just 29 second-half points. Jack McVeigh was outstanding in their previous meeting with Perth, pouring in 36 points and eight three-pointers in a 100–92 road win, while Keanu Pinder continues to provide an important presence inside.
 Perth have also rediscovered some momentum, bouncing back from three consecutive defeats with home victories over Tasmania (98–92) and Illawarra (111–100) in Round 9. Kristian Doolittle remains their most influential all-round player, while Elijah Pepper and Dylan Windler provide valuable perimeter scoring. The Wildcats' offence looked considerably more dangerous against the Hawks, although defensive consistency remains a concern, particularly with Jo Lual-Acuil Jr. sidelined through injury.
 This shapes as a fascinating contest between two teams arriving in improved form. Cairns will take confidence from their recent victory in Perth and have the advantage of playing at home, but the Wildcats have shown they can score heavily when their offence clicks. The Taipans' improved defensive intensity and McVeigh's scoring threat could prove decisive in what looks a closely contested matchup.
 FULL PREVIEW -> 
 QUICK PREVIEW 
 Tasmania JackJumpers v Illawarra Hawks
 SAT 21 NOV | 5:30pm AEDT | MyState Bank Arena, Hobart 
 Tasmania return home on Saturday afternoon riding high after a remarkable victory over Brisbane in Round 9, with Kody Stattmann emerging as the unlikely hero. The reserve guard exploded for an incredible 28 points, stepping up when the injury-ravaged JackJumpers desperately needed someone to provide an offensive spark. Scott Roth's side continue to defy expectations despite missing several regular rotation players, with Taran Armstrong, Josh Bannan, Dakota Mathias and Will Magnay carrying enormous responsibility. Stattmann's breakout performance provides a welcome boost and demonstrates the remarkable resilience that has become a trademark of Tasmania's season.
 Illawarra travel to Hobart looking to build on their recent improvement, with the Hawks showing considerable offensive firepower in their 120–110 victory over South East Melbourne in Round 9. Kelan Martin, Tyler Harvey and Makur Maker provide multiple scoring threats, while Will Hickey's playmaking gives Illawarra another important attacking dimension. However, the Hawks have struggled to maintain defensive consistency, and their ability to contain Tasmania's increasingly confident supporting players will be crucial.
 The JackJumpers will be eager to capitalise on their home-court advantage, particularly with the confidence gained from their victory over Brisbane. While Stattmann's 28-point performance was extraordinary, expecting him to reproduce those numbers would be unrealistic, and Tasmania's limited depth remains a genuine concern. Illawarra have the scoring talent to challenge the JackJumpers, but Tasmania's defensive discipline, rebounding strength and remarkable ability to overcome adversity make them difficult to oppose at home.

 FULL MATCH PREVIEW 
 Melbourne United v New Zealand Breakers
 SAT 21 NOV | 7:30pm AEDT | John Cain Arena, Melbourne 
 Melbourne United return to John Cain Arena on Saturday night looking to consolidate their position among the NBL's leading teams. Cole Anthony and Josh Oduro have emerged as two of United's most influential players, providing a potent combination of perimeter scoring and interior strength. The experience of Chris Goulding, Shea Ili and Joe Ingles gives Melbourne considerable depth, although their recent defeat to Adelaide exposed some defensive vulnerabilities. United will be confident of responding at home, particularly after recording a convincing 94–74 victory over New Zealand earlier this month.
 The Breakers enter Round 10 with a significant addition to their lineup, having signed former South East Melbourne Phoenix import Skylar Mays following the season-ending injury to Parker Jackson-Cartwright. Mays provides much-needed scoring ability and playmaking alongside Sam Mennenga and Dejan Vasiljevic, who recently exploded for 36 points against Brisbane. The American guard faces his former Phoenix teammates on Wednesday before travelling to Melbourne for Saturday's clash, giving him two games in quick succession to settle into New Zealand's system. His arrival could significantly improve the Breakers' offensive balance, although integrating a new import midway through the season presents challenges.
 Melbourne deserve favouritism given their superior depth, defensive structure and home-court advantage, but New Zealand could prove more dangerous with Mays providing another genuine offensive threat. The Breakers will need Mennenga to establish himself inside and Vasiljevic to continue his strong perimeter shooting, while Mays' ability to create opportunities for teammates could help ease the burden on their existing guards. United's combination of Anthony and Oduro should still give them the edge, particularly if they can control the rebounding battle and force New Zealand into difficult shots.
 FULL PREVIEW COMING SOON 
 QUICK PREVIEW 
 South East Melbourne Phoenix v Cairns Taipans
 SUN 22 NOV | 3:00pm AEDT | John Cain Arena, Melbourne 
 South East Melbourne complete their Round 10 double-header on Sunday afternoon against a Cairns side that has demonstrated considerable improvement this season. The Phoenix possess plenty of offensive talent through Nathan Sobey, D'Shawn Schwartz and Angus Glover, but their inability to maintain defensive intensity has been a recurring problem. The departure of Skylar Mays has also created additional responsibility for the remaining guards, with Dash Daniels likely to play an increasingly important role.
 Cairns will be playing their second game of the round after hosting Perth on Friday night. Jack McVeigh has been the driving force behind the Taipans' offence, while Keanu Pinder provides valuable scoring, rebounding and athleticism inside. The Taipans have shown they can challenge quality opposition when their outside shooting is working, although their own defensive inconsistency has contributed to several disappointing results.
 This shapes as a potentially entertaining contest between two teams capable of producing explosive offensive performances. South East Melbourne will look to use their home-court advantage and perimeter shooting to control the game, while Cairns have the versatility to attack both inside and outside. With neither team particularly reliable defensively, the total points market could be worth investigating once the opening line is available.
 BETTING TIP: To be confirmed once odds and updated team news are available. 
 FULL MATCH PREVIEW 
 Brisbane Bullets v Sydney Kings
 SUN 22 NOV | 5:00pm AEDT | Brisbane Entertainment Centre 
 Brisbane close Round 10 with a challenging home assignment against Sydney, looking to establish greater consistency after a frustrating opening to the season. The Bullets have demonstrated considerable offensive potential, particularly through Raul Neto's playmaking and the interior scoring of Tyrell Harrison. Nate Hinton has also provided valuable energy, rebounding and versatility, but defensive inconsistency and injuries have repeatedly undermined Brisbane's ability to convert promising performances into victories.
 Sydney have established themselves as one of the NBL's strongest teams, with Kendric Davis directing an offence that also features Torrey Craig, Xavier Cooks and Makuach Maluach. The Kings have been particularly impressive defensively, combining strong rebounding with the ability to control the tempo and restrict opposition scoring. Their greater depth and experience make them dangerous opponents, even when their outside shooting is not functioning at its best.
 The battle between Neto and Davis should be a major attraction, with both guards capable of creating opportunities for teammates and taking over offensively. Brisbane will need Harrison to establish himself inside while limiting Sydney's transition scoring and second-chance opportunities. The Kings deserve favouritism based on their overall consistency, but Brisbane's home-court advantage and offensive talent could make this more competitive than their respective ladder positions suggest.
